statement: Main technical risk: elapsed time between query date and version timestamp is not the legal validity relation. A monotone proximity score selects the temporally nearest version, which may not be the version in force. Prior et al. report that temporal validity must be a hard constraint, so a soft decay term may be technically the wrong signal for the stated legal goal even if it helps on average in non-legal settings.

evidence.quote: smaller differences in time result in a larger score
take into account the temporal validity of a statute as a hard constraint
